summary: Above the Gira river's full hairpin bend on the Girmal approach, a forest-department deck. The interior drive's classic tea-and-view halt.
description:
A few kilometres before Girmal falls, the Gira river swings through a complete U-turn in its forested valley, and the forest department has built the viewpoint exactly above the bend. The geometry is the show: the river arrives, wraps around a wooded spur and leaves the way it came, with ridgelines stacking behind it, in monsoon the whole loop runs brown-white under moving cloud, and Gujarat Tourism's own material rates the spot a highlight of the Dangs.

It has grown into the interior loop's natural halt. An Eco-Development Committee restaurant serves food through the peak monsoon season (tea and coffee only in the off months), and the small Girli Lodges next to it offer four basic rooms with attached bathrooms at around ₹500 a night: worth knowing if you want to sleep beside the bend rather than drive back to Ahwa.

Come en route Girmal rather than as a destination in itself: ten minutes for the view and chai, longer if the cloud theatre is running. The deck is railed and easy for all ages.
highlights: Full U-turn of the Gira river seen from directly above
Girli Lodges, four basic rooms by the viewpoint
The natural halt on the Girmal falls approach

modes.road: On the Girmal approach: Ahwa to Subir, on to Nishana check-post, then the Girmal village road. The viewpoint comes before the falls
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Roadside viewpoint, steps from parking to the railed deck
access.road_condition: Single-lane forest road with rough patches after the check-post

visit.notes: The restaurant runs full service in peak monsoon and tea/coffee only off-season.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon for the full river loop and cloud; the bend still reads well into early winter, thin by summer.

experience.photography_notes: Wide frames take the whole hairpin; monsoon mist opens and closes the view in minutes, wait it out with chai.

amenities.food: Eco-Development Committee restaurant at the deck, meals in peak monsoon, tea/coffee otherwise

warnings: Stay behind the railing: the drop to the river bend is sheer
The approach road is single-lane; park fully off the carriageway

tips: Do it as the pause on the Girmal run: falls first if light matters to you, chai here after
Girli Lodges' four rooms make an offbeat overnight if Mahal campsite is full

nearby.note: The viewpoint sits on the falls approach
